title: Postcard and Summer
premise: Zephyrine Oyelaran has built a career on other people's voices, and her newest contract is her most dangerous: ghostwriting the memoirs of Adaeze Okonkwo-Bright, the publishing heiress whose family empire crushed Zephyrine's own mother's small press years ago. When Zephyrine needs a date to survive the Oyelaran family reunion in Lagos, she hires Temi, a charming stranger who turns out to be Adaeze's estranged nephew — planted by Adaeze to spy on the ghostwriter who knows too much about the old scandal. As fake affection curdles into something real, Zephyrine must choose between exposing the inheritance built on her mother's ruin and protecting the man who deceived her; in the end she publishes the truth under her own name, forfeits the fortune she could have extorted, and chooses Temi only after forgiving herself for the survival compromises that made her a ghost.
about_author: Odile Voss is the pen name of a former literary scout who spent a decade watching fortunes change hands in quiet conference rooms. She writes romances about people who mistake control for safety, from a coastal town she refuses to name.

chapters.title: The Muscle Theory
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. She signs a lucrative contract to ghostwrite publishing matriarch Adaeze Okonkwo-Bright's memoirs, telling herself the heart is trainable, containable — like any muscle. Flashback hints at her mother's failed press. Emotional beat: armored ambition masking an old wound.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. The family reunion looms: her aunt will announce the sale of the last piece of her mother's legacy. Zephyrine hires Temi, a warm, disarming stranger from a café, to pose as her boyfriend for one weekend. Beat: calculated risk dressed as convenience.

chapters.title: Rehearsal Dinner for Liars
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Their first rehearsal goes too well; Temi remembers details she never told him, touches her hand like it's habit. She files it under professionalism. Beat: the first crack in containment.

chapters.title: Dessert
chapters.summary: Dual POV. At the reunion, the fake date feels devastatingly real by dessert — until Temi's phone buzzes with a message from 'Aunty Ada.' Zephyrine sees the name. Beat: recognition, vertigo, silence chosen over confrontation.

chapters.title: The Nephew Clause
chapters.summary: Temi's POV. He confesses nothing; we learn he is Adaeze's estranged nephew, paid to vet the ghostwriter digging into the family archive. His guilt is genuine, his attraction more so. Beat: complicity with a conscience.

chapters.title: Interviews with a Fortress
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Memoir sessions with Adaeze become duels; the old woman deflects every question about Bright & Sons' acquisition of smaller presses. Zephyrine recognizes the technique — it's her own. Beat: hunter and mirror.

chapters.title: What Mother Kept
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. In her mother's storage boxes she finds correspondence proving Adaeze personally engineered the hostile buyout — and a letter her mother never sent, offering forgiveness. Beat: grief weaponized into purpose.

chapters.title: Rain on the Balcony
chapters.summary: Temi's POV. Temi and Zephyrine stop performing and start talking; he almost tells her everything, instead tells her half. The kiss is real and ruins them both. Beat: intimacy as exposure.

chapters.title: The Archive Room
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Granted access to the company archive for the memoir, she photographs documents linking the buyout to forged debts. Adaeze watches her do it and says nothing. Beat: dread dressed as permission.

chapters.title: Two Contracts
chapters.summary: Adaeze's POV (first time). Adaeze reveals she knows what Zephyrine found — and offers a counter-deal: bury the chapter, inherit a seat at the table, restore her mother's name with money instead of truth. Beat: temptation with impeccable manners.

chapters.title: Survival Is a Habit
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Zephyrine realizes how much of herself she has already sold to stay safe — the ghostwriting, the silence, now this. She drafts the buried chapter anyway, alone, at 3 a.m. Beat: self-confrontation begins.

chapters.title: The Man in the Middle
chapters.summary: Temi's POV. Adaeze orders Temi to steal Zephyrine's research or lose the family allowance he secretly sends his ailing father. He stalls, lies to both women, and hates himself fluently. Beat: the price of loyalty to the wrong ledger.

chapters.title: Postcard, Undated
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. She finds an old postcard among her mother's things — a summer snapshot of the two mothers together, friends before the betrayal. The inheritance she's chasing was once a friendship. Beat: sorrow complicating vengeance.

chapters.title: Confession by Candlelight
chapters.summary: Temi's POV. Cornered by his father's hospital bills, Temi tells Zephyrine everything: the hire, the spying, the theft he refused. She walks out. Beat: honesty arriving exactly too late.

chapters.title: The Ghost Speaks
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Humiliated and furious, Zephyrine nearly takes Adaeze's deal — the seat, the money, the restored name. She gets as far as the signature line. Beat: the darkest hour, pen hovering.

chapters.title: What the Mirror Owes
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Alone, she reads her mother's unsent forgiveness letter aloud and finally hears it as instruction, not accusation: forgive yourself first. She tears up the deal. Beat: the turn inward that makes the outward choice possible.

chapters.title: Boardroom Summer
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. At the annual Bright board meeting, Zephyrine stands uninvited and reads the forged-debt evidence aloud, naming Adaeze and implicating the system, not just the woman. Temi backs her with the archive keys. Beat: climax — truth as a public act.

chapters.title: Fallout
chapters.summary: Temi's POV. The empire fractures; Adaeze, cornered, chooses partial confession over ruin and dissolves the trust rather than let it be seized. Temi loses his allowance and gains his father's respect. Beat: consequences distributed fairly.

chapters.title: Byline
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Zephyrine publishes the story under her own name — no ghost, no fee — and turns down three offers to monetize the scandal. Her mother's press name is licensed, not sold, to a cooperative of young publishers. Beat: inheritance redefined.

chapters.title: The Long Way to Apologize
chapters.summary: Temi's POV. Temi shows up at Zephyrine's door with no contract, no cover story, and a summer's worth of postcards he wrote and never sent. She doesn't forgive him yet — but she lets him sit on the step. Beat: love rebuilt on terms, not surrender.

chapters.title: Muscle Memory
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Weeks later, Zephyrine admits the heart was never containable — only waiting. She writes Temi a real letter, the first thing signed in her own voice in years. Beat: tenderness earned through honesty.

chapters.title: Postcard and Summer
chapters.summary: Dual POV. One year on, at the reunion of the new cooperative press, Zephyrine and Temi arrive together — no pretense required. Her mother's postcard hangs framed above the door. Final beat: survival's price paid, inheritance claimed as story, not property.
